builtins.name: strlen
builtins.desc: Length of a string in bytes (not characters). For arrays use count().

params.name: $v
params.description: the string (bytes) or array (elements) to measure

builtins.returns: Number of bytes in the string, or number of elements in the array.

builtins.name: count
builtins.desc: Number of elements in an array, or length of a string. Aliased by sizeof().

params.name: $v
params.description: array to count, or string to measure

builtins.returns: Element count of the array, byte length of the string.

builtins.name: sizeof
builtins.desc: Alias of count(): elements in an array, bytes in a string.
builtins.returns: Same as count().

builtins.name: strtoupper
builtins.desc: Converts every ASCII letter in the string to uppercase.
builtins.returns: The string with every ASCII letter uppercased.

builtins.name: strtolower
builtins.desc: Converts every ASCII letter in the string to lowercase.
builtins.returns: The string with every ASCII letter lowercased.

builtins.name: ucfirst
builtins.desc: Uppercases the first character of the string, leaves the rest untouched.
builtins.returns: The string with its first character uppercased.

builtins.name: lcfirst
builtins.desc: Lowercases the first character of the string, leaves the rest untouched.
builtins.returns: The string with its first character lowercased.

builtins.name: trim
builtins.desc: Strips leading and trailing whitespace (space, tab, newline, CR, NUL).
builtins.returns: The string without leading or trailing whitespace.

builtins.name: ltrim
builtins.desc: Strips leading whitespace only. Optional second argument: character list to strip.
builtins.returns: The string without leading whitespace.

builtins.name: rtrim
builtins.desc: Strips trailing whitespace only. Alias: chop(). Optional second argument: character list.
builtins.returns: The string without trailing whitespace.

builtins.name: chop
builtins.desc: Alias of rtrim(): strips trailing whitespace.
builtins.returns: Same as rtrim().

builtins.name: strrev
builtins.desc: Reverses the string byte by byte.
builtins.returns: The string reversed byte by byte.

builtins.name: str_repeat
builtins.desc: Repeats the string n times: str_repeat("ab", 3) -> "ababab".
builtins.returns: The string repeated $n times (empty when n <= 0).

builtins.name: str_pad
builtins.desc: Pads the string to the given length with a pad string (default " "), repeated on the right.
builtins.returns: The string padded on the right with repeats of $pad up to $len bytes; unchanged when already longer.

builtins.name: str_replace
builtins.desc: str_replace($search, $replace, $subject) — replaces every occurrence of $search in $subject.
builtins.returns: The string with every occurrence of $search replaced by $replace.

builtins.name: substr
builtins.desc: substr($s, $start[, $len]) — extracts up to $len bytes starting at $start. Negative $start counts from the end; omitted $len means "to the end".

params.name: $len
params.description: maximum length; omitted = to the end

builtins.returns: The extracted substring.

builtins.name: strstr
builtins.desc: Returns the part of $haystack from the first occurrence of $needle to the end, or false if not found.
builtins.returns: The part of $haystack starting at the first $needle, or false when not found.

builtins.name: strchr
builtins.desc: Alias of strstr().
builtins.returns: Alias of strstr().

builtins.name: strpos
builtins.desc: Byte position of the first occurrence of $needle in $haystack, or false when absent. Use !== false to test.
builtins.returns: 0-based byte position of the first occurrence, or false when not found. Always compare with !== false — position 0 is falsy!

builtins.name: str_contains
builtins.desc: true when $needle occurs anywhere in $haystack (PHP 8 style, no position needed).
builtins.returns: true when $needle occurs anywhere in $haystack.

builtins.name: str_starts_with
builtins.desc: true when $haystack begins with $needle.
builtins.returns: true when $haystack begins with $needle.

builtins.name: str_ends_with
builtins.desc: true when $haystack ends with $needle.
builtins.returns: true when $haystack ends with $needle.

builtins.name: strcmp
builtins.desc: Byte-wise comparison: returns < 0, 0, or > 0 as $a sorts before, equal to, or after $b.
builtins.returns: < 0 when $a sorts before $b, 0 when equal, > 0 when $a sorts after $b.

builtins.name: strncmp
builtins.desc: Like strcmp() but compares at most the first n bytes (third argument).
builtins.returns: Like strcmp(), limited to the first $n bytes.

builtins.name: strncasecmp
builtins.desc: Case-insensitive strncmp(): first n bytes, returns -1/0/1 style result.
builtins.returns: Case-insensitive strncmp().

builtins.name: strcasecmp
builtins.desc: Case-insensitive strcmp().
builtins.returns: Case-insensitive strcmp().

builtins.name: explode
builtins.desc: explode($separator, $s) - splits the string at every separator into an array. An empty separator splits into single characters (UTF-8 safe): explode("", "Hilf") -> ["H","i","l","f"].
builtins.returns: Array of the pieces between separators.

builtins.name: split
builtins.desc: Alias of explode(); an empty separator splits the string into single characters.
builtins.returns: Alias of explode().

builtins.name: implode
builtins.desc: Joins array elements with a glue string: implode($glue, $arr) or implode($arr).
builtins.returns: All elements joined by $glue.

builtins.name: join
builtins.desc: Alias of implode().
builtins.returns: Alias of implode().

builtins.name: nl2br
builtins.desc:
Inserts "
" before every newline. Newlines are kept.
builtins.returns:
The string with "
" inserted before every newline (newlines kept).

builtins.name: number_format
builtins.desc: Formats a number with grouped thousands: number_format($n[, $decimals[, $dec_point, $thousands_sep]]). Defaults: 0 decimals, ".", ",".
builtins.returns: The formatted number string.

builtins.name: unset
builtins.desc: unset($arr["k"]) removes the key from the array; unset($var) is not needed for locals.
builtins.returns: Removes the element from the array.

builtins.name: json_encode
builtins.desc: Encodes a value as JSON. Flags: JSON_PRETTY_PRINT (indented), JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES (keep /), JSON_NUMERIC_CHECK, JSON_FORCE_OBJECT. Combine with |.
builtins.returns: JSON string.

builtins.name: json_encode_pretty
builtins.desc: json_encode() with JSON_PRETTY_PRINT pre-applied — convenience wrapper.
builtins.returns: json_encode() with JSON_PRETTY_PRINT pre-applied.

builtins.name: json_decode
builtins.desc: Decodes a JSON string into arrays/maps/scalars. Optional second argument ($assoc) is accepted for PHP compatibility and ignored.

params.name: $assoc
params.description: accepted for PHP compatibility; maps come as maps either way

builtins.returns: The decoded value (maps as maps, scalars as scalars); null on invalid JSON.

builtins.name: preg_match
builtins.desc: preg_match($pattern, $subject[, &$matches]) — tries the pattern once on $subject. Returns 1 and fills $matches (index 0 = full match, 1..n = capture groups) on success, false on no match or bad pattern. Patterns use /.../ delimiters with flags i (case-insensitive), s (dotall), m (multiline).

params.name: $pattern
params.description: /…/ pattern with optional flags i, s, m

params.name: $matches
params.description: out-parameter: filled with the match (index 0) and capture groups (1..n)

builtins.returns: 1 and fills $matches on success; false on no match or invalid pattern.

builtins.name: preg_match_all
builtins.desc: preg_match_all($pattern, $subject[, &$matches]) — finds every non-overlapping match. Returns the number of matches and fills $matches with one array per match (each like preg_match's $matches).
builtins.returns: Number of matches found; fills $matches with one sub-array per match.

builtins.name: preg_replace
builtins.desc: preg_replace($pattern, $replacement, $subject) — replaces every match. $replacement may reference captures as $1, $2, … Returns the modified string.
builtins.returns: The string with every match replaced.

builtins.name: preg_split
builtins.desc: preg_split($pattern, $subject) — splits $subject at every match of the pattern and returns the pieces as an array.
builtins.returns: Array of the pieces between matches.

builtins.name: preg_grep
builtins.desc: preg_grep($pattern, $array) — returns the elements of $array that match the pattern (keys are re-indexed 0..n).
builtins.returns: The elements that match the pattern, re-indexed 0..n.

builtins.name: sha256
builtins.desc: SHA-256 hash as 64-char hex. The general-purpose hash of this runtime.
builtins.returns: 64-character hex SHA-256 digest — the standard hash of this runtime.

builtins.name: hash_hmac
builtins.desc: hash_hmac("sha256", $data, $key) — keyed HMAC-SHA256 for signing messages.
builtins.returns: HMAC digest as hex — proves the message came from someone holding $key.

builtins.name: password_hash
builtins.desc: Creates a salted password hash ($hphp$4096$salt$digest, PBKDF2-SHA256, 4096 rounds). Store this string; never store plain passwords.
builtins.returns: Storable hash string ($hphp$4096$salt$digest, PBKDF2-SHA256). The salt is random per call.
builtins.example:
$h = password_hash("correct horse");
echo strlen($h) > 40 && password_verify("correct horse", $h) ? "hash-ok" : "hash-bad";

builtins.name: password_verify
builtins.desc: password_verify($plain, $hash) — recomputes the digest with the hash's salt and compares timing-safely. true when the password matches.
builtins.returns: true when the password matches the hash (timing-safe).

builtins.name: random_bytes
builtins.desc: random_bytes($n) — $n cryptographically secure random bytes as a raw binary string (max 1024).
builtins.returns: $n cryptographically secure random bytes as a binary string.

builtins.name: hash_equals
builtins.desc: Timing-safe string comparison for verifying hashes/signatures — always use it for secrets instead of ===.
builtins.returns: true when equal — compared in constant time so timing attacks fail. Always use for secrets.

builtins.name: mktime
builtins.sig: mktime(int $hour, int $minute, int $second, int $month, int $day, int $year): int
builtins.desc: mktime($h, $m, $s, $month, $day, $year) — builds a Unix timestamp from local date/time parts.
builtins.returns: Unix timestamp for that local date/time.
builtins.authoredSignature: int $hour, int $minute, int $second, int $month, int $day, int $year

builtins.name: strtotime
builtins.desc: Parses a date/time string ("2024-03-15 12:30:00", "2024-03-15", "12:30:00") into a Unix timestamp; 0 on failure.
builtins.returns: Unix timestamp, or 0 when unparseable.

builtins.name: http_post
builtins.desc: http_post($url, $body[, $headers]) — HTTP POST with the body string and optional header lines (e.g. "Content-Type: application/json"). Same return shape as http_get().
builtins.returns: Same map as http_get(), or false on failure.

builtins.name: parse_url
builtins.desc: parse_url($url) — map with scheme, user, host, port, path, query, fragment; missing parts are empty strings, port defaults to 80/443.
builtins.returns: Map with scheme, user, host, port, path, query, fragment; missing parts are empty, port defaults to 80/443.

builtins.name: http_build_query
builtins.desc: Turns a map into an urlencoded query string: ["a" => "x y"] → "a=x+y".
builtins.returns: URL-encoded query string.

builtins.name: mysql_connect
builtins.sig: mysql_connect(string $host[, int $port, string $user, string $pass, string $db]): mixed
builtins.desc: mysql_connect($host[, $port[, $user[, $pass[, $db]]]]) — opens a MySQL/MariaDB connection (native wire protocol, TCP). Returns a connection handle or false.
builtins.returns: Connection handle for mysql_query/mysql_exec, or false on failure.

builtins.name: mysql_query
builtins.desc: mysql_query($conn, $sql) — runs a SELECT/SHOW and returns the rows as an array of maps (column name => value), false on error. For INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE use mysql_exec().
builtins.returns: Rows as array of maps (column name => value), false on error.
builtins.example: echo "rows = mysql_query($c, "SELECT id, name FROM users");";
builtins.exampleOutput: rows = mysql_query($c, "SELECT id, name FROM users");

builtins.name: mysql_exec
builtins.desc: mysql_exec($conn, $sql) — runs a statement and returns the number of affected rows, false on error.
builtins.returns: Number of affected rows, false on error.
builtins.example: echo "affected = mysql_exec($c, "DELETE FROM logs WHERE old = 1");";
builtins.exampleOutput: affected = mysql_exec($c, "DELETE FROM logs WHERE old = 1");

builtins.name: mysql_insert_id
builtins.desc: AUTO_INCREMENT value generated by the last INSERT on this connection.
builtins.returns: AUTO_INCREMENT value of the last INSERT on this connection.

builtins.name: mysql_close
builtins.desc: Closes the MySQL connection.
builtins.returns: true when closed.

builtins.name: mysql_escape
builtins.desc: Escapes a string for safe embedding in SQL text (see the crypto group entry).

params.name: $s
params.description: raw string going into SQL text

builtins.returns: Escaped string (' " \ NUL) safe for SQL literals.

builtins.name: md5
builtins.desc: MD5 hash as 32-char hex. Fast but broken for security — checksums only.
builtins.returns: 32-character hex MD5 digest. Broken for security — checksums only.

builtins.name: sha1
builtins.desc: SHA-1 hash as 40-char hex. Also legacy — prefer sha256().
builtins.returns: 40-character hex SHA-1 digest (legacy — prefer sha256).

builtins.name: crc32
builtins.desc: CRC-32 checksum of the data as an integer — detects accidental corruption, not tampering.
builtins.returns: CRC-32 checksum as integer — detects accidental corruption.

builtins.name: base64_encode
builtins.desc: Encodes bytes as Base64 text (with = padding) — for safe transport in JSON, URLs-after-urlencode, etc.
builtins.returns: Base64 text (with = padding).

builtins.name: base64_decode
builtins.desc: Decodes Base64 back to raw bytes. Invalid characters are skipped.
builtins.returns: The decoded raw bytes; invalid characters are skipped.

builtins.name: urlencode
builtins.desc: Encodes a string for use in a query string: space becomes +, reserved chars become %XX.
builtins.returns: Encoded text: space becomes +, reserved characters become %XX.

builtins.name: urldecode
builtins.desc: Inverse of urlencode().
builtins.returns: Decoded text.

builtins.name: htmlentities
builtins.desc: Converts & " ' < > (and more) to their HTML entities so the string is safe to embed as text.
builtins.returns: The text with HTML-critical characters converted to entities.

builtins.name: htmlspecialchars
builtins.desc: Converts only the five HTML-critical characters & " ' < > to entities.
builtins.returns: The text with only the five HTML-critical characters (& " ' < >) escaped.

builtins.name: sprintf
builtins.desc: printf-style formatting that returns the string. Supports %d %s %f %x %o %b %e %c, width, precision and "-" left-align.
builtins.returns: The formatted string. Specifiers: %d %s %f %x %o %b %e %c, with width, precision and "-" left-align.

builtins.name: printf
builtins.desc: Like sprintf() but prints the result and returns its length.
builtins.returns: Prints the formatted string; returns its length.

builtins.name: vsprintf
builtins.desc: sprintf() with the arguments taken from an array.
builtins.returns: sprintf() with values from an array.

builtins.name: ord
builtins.desc: Byte value of the first character of the string (0–255).

params.name: $s
params.description: string; only the first byte is used

builtins.returns: Byte value (0–255) of the first character.

builtins.name: chr
builtins.desc: One-character string for the given byte value.
builtins.returns: One-character string for that byte.

builtins.name: bin2hex
builtins.desc: Hexadecimal representation of the bytes, two chars per byte: bin2hex("AB") → "4142".
builtins.returns: Hex string, two characters per byte.

builtins.name: hex2bin
builtins.desc: Decodes a hexadecimal string back into raw bytes.
builtins.returns: The decoded raw bytes.

builtins.name: str_split
builtins.desc: str_split($s[, $len]) - cuts the string into chunks of $len characters (default 1) and returns them as an array.
builtins.returns: Array of chunks.

builtins.name: ucwords
builtins.desc: Uppercases the first letter of every whitespace-separated word.
builtins.returns: The string with the first letter of every word uppercased.

builtins.name: wordwrap
builtins.desc: Wraps a string to a given width by inserting breaks (default "\n") at word boundaries.
builtins.returns: The string wrapped at word boundaries.
builtins.example:
echo wordwrap("holy php makes coding holy again", 12), "
";
builtins.exampleOutput:
holy php
makes coding
holy again

builtins.name: similar_text
builtins.desc: Number of matching characters between the two strings (a rough similarity measure).
builtins.returns: Number of matching characters — a rough similarity measure.

builtins.name: levenshtein
builtins.desc: Edit distance (insertions, deletions, substitutions) between the two strings.
builtins.returns: Edit distance: minimum insertions + deletions + substitutions to turn $a into $b.

builtins.name: array
builtins.desc: Creates an array from the given values (or "key" => value pairs). Usually written as the [...] literal instead.
builtins.returns: The array built from the arguments. Prefer the [...] literal.

builtins.name: array_keys
builtins.desc: Returns all keys of the array as a new list array.
builtins.returns: List of all keys.

builtins.name: array_values
builtins.desc: Returns all values of the array as a freshly indexed list (0..n-1).
builtins.returns: List of all values, freshly indexed 0..n-1.

builtins.name: array_merge
builtins.desc: Merges two or more arrays; later arrays overwrite string keys of earlier ones, numeric keys are appended.
builtins.returns: One merged array: later string keys overwrite, numeric keys append.

builtins.name: array_slice
builtins.desc: array_slice($arr, $offset[, $length]) — extracts a section of the array. Negative $offset counts from the end.
builtins.returns: The extracted section as a new array.

builtins.name: array_reverse
builtins.desc: Returns the array with elements in reverse order.
builtins.returns: The elements in reverse order.

builtins.name: array_sum
builtins.desc: Sum of all numeric values in the array (non-numerics count as 0).
builtins.returns: Sum of all values (non-numerics count as 0).

builtins.name: array_product
builtins.desc: Product of all numeric values in the array.
builtins.returns: Product of all values.

builtins.name: array_unique
builtins.desc: Removes duplicate values, keeping the first occurrence of each.
builtins.returns: The array without duplicate values (first occurrence wins).

builtins.name: in_array
builtins.desc: in_array($needle, $haystack) — true when the value occurs in the array.
builtins.returns: true when the value occurs in the array.

builtins.name: array_key_exists
builtins.desc: true when $key exists in the array (also for string keys and null values).
builtins.returns: true when the key exists — also when its value is null (unlike isset).

builtins.name: isset
builtins.desc: isset($arr["k"]) — true when the key exists and the value is not null.
builtins.returns: true when the variable is set and not null.

builtins.name: range
builtins.desc: range($start, $end) — list of integers from $start to $end inclusive (also counts down).
builtins.returns: List of integers from $start to $end; counts down when $end < $start.

builtins.name: compact
builtins.desc: Builds an array from the named local variables: compact("a", "b") → ["a" => $a, "b" => $b].
builtins.returns: Map variable-name => value for every existing local with that name.

builtins.name: array_column
builtins.desc: array_column($rows, $col) — picks one column out of an array of maps, indexed 0..n.

params.name: $col
params.description: key to pick from every row

builtins.returns: List of the picked column values.

builtins.name: array_chunk
builtins.desc: array_chunk($arr, $size) — splits the array into chunks of at most $size elements.
builtins.returns: Array of arrays, each with at most $size elements.

builtins.name: array_pad
builtins.desc: array_pad($arr, $size, $value) — grows the array to $size by filling with $value (negative size pads left).

params.name: $size
params.description: target size (negative pads on the left)

builtins.returns: The array grown to $size elements.

builtins.name: array_replace
builtins.desc: array_replace($a, $b, …) — elements of later arrays overwrite those of earlier ones, keys preserved.
builtins.returns: The base array with later arrays overwriting by key (keys preserved).

builtins.name: array_fill_keys
builtins.desc: array_fill_keys(["a","b"], $v) — map with those keys, each mapped to $v.
builtins.returns: Map with each key mapped to $value.

builtins.name: array_key_first
builtins.desc: First key of the array (null when empty).
builtins.returns: The first key, or null when empty.

builtins.name: array_key_last
builtins.desc: Last key of the array (null when empty).
builtins.returns: The last key, or null when empty.

builtins.name: usort
builtins.desc: usort($arr, $cmp) — sorts by value in place using a comparator closure returning -1/0/1.
builtins.returns: true; the array is sorted in place.

builtins.name: uasort
builtins.desc: usort with key association preserved (for maps).
builtins.returns: true; sorts by value while keeping key association.

builtins.name: uksort
builtins.desc: Sorts the map in place by key using a comparator closure.
builtins.returns: true; sorts by key using the closure.

builtins.name: array_walk
builtins.desc: array_walk($arr, $fn) — calls $fn($value, $key) for every element; the closure may modify $value via a by-ref parameter.

params.name: $fn
params.description: callback fn(value, key) — receives COPIES, not references

builtins.returns: true; calls $fn for every element.

builtins.name: array_walk_recursive
builtins.desc: Like array_walk() but descends into nested arrays.
builtins.returns: true; visits leaves of nested arrays only.

builtins.name: substr_count
builtins.desc: Counts how many times $needle occurs in $haystack.
builtins.returns: How many times $needle occurs in $haystack.

builtins.name: str_shuffle
builtins.desc: Randomly shuffles the characters of the string (not cryptographically secure).
builtins.returns: The characters in random order (not cryptographically secure).

builtins.name: strip_tags
builtins.desc: Removes HTML and PHP tags from the string.
builtins.returns: The text without HTML tags.

builtins.name: html_entity_decode
builtins.desc: Inverse of htmlentities(): "&" becomes "&" again.
builtins.returns: The decoded text ("&" becomes "&").

builtins.name: array_map
builtins.desc: array_map($fn, $arr[, $arr2, …]) — applies the closure to every element and returns the results. With several arrays the closure gets one argument per array.

params.name: $args
params.description: more arrays — one value per array is passed to $fn

builtins.returns: New array with the transformed values.

builtins.name: array_filter
builtins.desc: array_filter($arr[, $fn]) — keeps elements where $fn returns true; without $fn keeps all truthy elements. Keys are preserved.

params.name: $fn
params.description: predicate; without it, truthy elements are kept

builtins.returns: The elements where $fn returned true (keys preserved).

builtins.name: array_reduce
builtins.desc: array_reduce($arr, $fn[, $initial]) — folds the array left-to-right: $fn($carry, $item).
builtins.returns: The final carry after folding left-to-right.

builtins.name: array_flip
builtins.desc: Swaps keys and values: ["a" => 1] becomes [1 => "a"].
builtins.returns: Map with keys and values swapped.

builtins.name: array_fill
builtins.desc: array_fill($start, $num, $value) — $num copies of $value starting at index $start.
builtins.returns: Array with $num copies of $value starting at $start.

builtins.name: array_combine
builtins.desc: array_combine($keys, $values) — builds a map using one array as keys and the other as values.
builtins.returns: Map built from the two lists.

builtins.name: array_diff
builtins.desc: array_diff($a, $b, …) — values of $a that do not appear in any other array.

params.name: $args
params.description: first the base array, then arrays of values to exclude

builtins.returns: Values of the first array that appear in none of the others.

builtins.name: array_intersect
builtins.desc: array_intersect($a, $b, …) — values of $a that appear in all other arrays.

params.name: $args
params.description: first the base array, then arrays to intersect with

builtins.returns: Values of the first array that appear in all the others.

builtins.name: array_push
builtins.desc: Appends one or more values to the end of the array; returns the new count. $arr[] = v is preferred.
builtins.returns: New element count. $arr[] = v does the same for one value.

builtins.name: array_pop
builtins.desc: Removes and returns the last element of the array (null when empty).
builtins.returns: The removed last element (null when empty).

builtins.name: array_shift
builtins.desc: Removes and returns the first element, re-indexing the rest (null when empty).
builtins.returns: The removed first element; the rest is re-indexed.

builtins.name: array_unshift
builtins.desc: Prepends one or more values to the front of the array; returns the new count.
builtins.returns: New element count.

builtins.name: array_splice
builtins.desc: array_splice($arr, $offset[, $length[, $replacement]]) — removes a section and optionally replaces it; returns the removed elements.
builtins.returns: Array of the removed elements; the input array is modified.

builtins.name: shuffle
builtins.desc: Randomly reorders the array in place (not cryptographically secure).
builtins.returns: true; the elements are reordered randomly (not crypto-secure).

builtins.name: sort
builtins.desc: Sorts the array in place by value, ascending, re-indexing 0..n.
builtins.returns: true; sorted ascending by value, re-indexed 0..n.

builtins.name: rsort
builtins.desc: Sorts the array in place by value, descending, re-indexing.
builtins.returns: true; sorted descending by value.

builtins.name: ksort
builtins.desc: Sorts the map in place by key, ascending, keeping key/value association.

params.name: $a
params.description: map to sort by key (by reference)

builtins.returns: true; sorted ascending by key, key/value association kept.

builtins.name: krsort
builtins.desc: Sorts the map in place by key, descending.

params.name: $a
params.description: map to sort by key (by reference)

builtins.returns: true; sorted descending by key.

builtins.name: asort
builtins.desc: Sorts the map in place by value, ascending, keeping key/value association.

params.name: $a
params.description: map to sort by value (by reference)

builtins.returns: true; sorted ascending by value, keys kept.

builtins.name: array_search
builtins.desc: Returns the key of the first element equal to $needle, or false when not found.
builtins.returns: The key of the first match, or false when not found.

builtins.name: end

builtins.returns: Sets the text color.

builtins.name: ui_font
builtins.sig: ui_font(int $handle, int $size[, bool $bold, bool $italic, string $family]): int
builtins.desc: ui_font($handle, $size[, $bold[, $italic[, $family]]]) — sets a control's font.
builtins.returns: Sets the control's font.

builtins.name: ui_menu
builtins.desc: Creates a menu bar / menu for a window.

params.name: $title
params.description: menu title in the menu bar

builtins.returns: Menu handle for ui_menu_item/ui_menu_sep.

builtins.name: ui_menu_item
builtins.desc: Appends an item to a menu; returns its handle (for ui_on callbacks).
builtins.returns: Item handle — attach a callback with ui_on($item, "click", …).

builtins.name: ui_menu_sep
builtins.desc: Appends a separator line to a menu.
builtins.returns: Adds a separator line.

builtins.name: ui_menu_check
builtins.desc: ui_menu_check($handle, $checked) — checkable menu item state.
builtins.returns: Sets the checkmark of a menu item.

builtins.name: ui_on
builtins.desc: ui_on($handle, $event, $callback) — registers a closure for events: "click", "change", "select", "close", … The closure receives event-specific arguments.
builtins.returns: Registers an event handler.

builtins.name: ui_timer
builtins.desc: ui_timer($ms, $callback) — runs the closure every $ms milliseconds until ui_quit().
builtins.returns: Starts a repeating timer until ui_quit().

builtins.name: ui_msg
builtins.desc: ui_msg($win, $title, $text[, $type]) — message box. $type: 0=info 1=warning 2=error 3=question.
builtins.returns: Shows a message box (blocks until dismissed).

builtins.name: ui_open_file
builtins.desc: Opens the platform file-open dialog; returns the chosen path or false.
builtins.returns: Chosen file path, or false when cancelled.

builtins.name: ui_save_file
builtins.desc: Opens the platform save-file dialog; returns the chosen path or false.
builtins.returns: Chosen save path, or false when cancelled.

builtins.name: ui_pick_folder
builtins.desc: Folder-picker dialog; returns the path or false.
builtins.returns: Chosen folder path, or false when cancelled.

builtins.name: ui_pick_color
builtins.desc: Color-picker dialog; returns the RGB int or false.
builtins.returns: Chosen color as RGB int, or false when cancelled.

builtins.name: ui_clip_set
builtins.desc: Copies text to the system clipboard.
builtins.returns: Copies to the system clipboard.

builtins.name: ui_clip_get
builtins.desc: Reads text from the system clipboard.
builtins.returns: Current clipboard text.

builtins.name: ui_theme
builtins.desc: ui_theme($win, $bg, $surface, $elevated, $text, $muted, $accent, $onAccent, $border, $radius, $fontPt, $titlePt, $rowH, $dark) — sets the look of a window and every control in it.

builtins.name: ui_style
builtins.desc: ui_style($h, $role) — assigns a style role to a control, i.e. how it is painted.

builtins.name: ui_accent
builtins.desc: ui_accent($h, $rgb) — accent colour of a control, e.g. 0xFF8C00.

builtins.name: ui_radius
builtins.desc: ui_radius($h, $px) — corner radius of a control in pixels.

builtins.name: ui_range
builtins.desc: ui_range($h, $lo, $hi) — minimum and maximum of a slider or progress control.

builtins.name: ui_repaint
builtins.desc: ui_repaint($h) — schedules a redraw of the window/control.

builtins.name: ui_input_margin
builtins.desc: ui_input_margin($h, $left, $right) — insets the text of an edit control (room for an icon, e.g. in an address bar).

builtins.name: ui_raise
builtins.desc: ui_raise($h) — brings a window or control to the front.

builtins.name: ui_svg
builtins.desc: ui_svg($h, $source) — sets the SVG markup drawn by a picture control.

builtins.name: ui_picture
builtins.desc: ui_picture($h, $path) — loads an image file into a picture control.

builtins.name: ui_text_px
builtins.desc: ui_text_px($text, $pt, $bold) — measured width of that string in pixels.

builtins.name: ui_text_lines
builtins.desc: ui_text_lines($text, $pt, $bold, $maxWidth) — how many lines the text wraps to at that width.

builtins.name: ui_enabled
builtins.desc: ui_enabled($h) — true when the control still accepts input (ui_enable() toggles it).

builtins.name: ui_rect
builtins.desc: ui_rect($h) — [x, y, w, h] of a control in its parent's coordinates, or null.

builtins.name: ui_client_size
builtins.desc: ui_client_size($win) — [width, height] of a window's client area.

builtins.name: ui_scroll
builtins.desc: ui_scroll($win, $dy, $to) — scrolls by $dy (or to $to) and returns [offset, contentHeight, viewportHeight].

builtins.name: ui_count
builtins.desc: ui_count($h) — number of items in a list or combo control.

builtins.name: ui_progress_get
builtins.desc: ui_progress_get($h) — current value of a progress bar.

builtins.name: ui_hwnd
builtins.desc: ui_hwnd($win) — the native window handle (HWND) of a window.

builtins.name: ui_font_new
builtins.desc: ui_font_new($family, $pt, $bold, $italic) — creates a font for canvas drawing and returns its id.

builtins.name: ui_font_width
builtins.desc: ui_font_width($font, $text) — width of that string in the given font, in pixels.

builtins.name: ui_font_height
builtins.desc: ui_font_height($font) — line height of the given font, in pixels.

builtins.name: ui_draw_clear
builtins.desc: ui_draw_clear($cv, $rgb) — fills the whole canvas with one colour.

builtins.name: ui_draw_rect
builtins.desc: ui_draw_rect($cv, …) — draws a rectangle on the canvas.

builtins.name: ui_draw_round
builtins.desc: ui_draw_round($cv, …) — draws a rectangle with rounded corners on the canvas.

builtins.name: ui_draw_line
builtins.desc: ui_draw_line($cv, …) — draws a line on the canvas.

builtins.name: ui_draw_text
builtins.desc: ui_draw_text($cv, …) — draws text on the canvas with the current font and colour.

builtins.name: ui_draw_clip
builtins.desc: ui_draw_clip($cv, …) — restricts further drawing to a rectangle.

builtins.name: ui_draw_unclip
builtins.desc: ui_draw_unclip($cv) — removes the clip rectangle again.

builtins.name: ui_canvas_size
builtins.desc: ui_canvas_size($cv) — [width, height] of the drawing surface in pixels.

builtins.name: ui_canvas_pixel
builtins.desc: ui_canvas_pixel($cv, $x, $y) — RGB value of the pixel at that position.

builtins.name: ui_canvas_invalidate
builtins.desc: ui_canvas_invalidate($cv, …) — marks a region dirty so it is repainted.

builtins.name: ui_canvas_flush
builtins.desc: ui_canvas_flush($cv) — pushes everything drawn since the last flush to the screen.

builtins.name: ui_cursor
builtins.desc: ui_cursor($cv, $shape) — sets the mouse cursor shown over the canvas.

builtins.name: shell_exec
builtins.desc: Runs an external command and returns its complete stdout as a string.
builtins.returns: Complete stdout of the command as a string.

builtins.name: exec
builtins.desc: Runs an external command, discards its output, returns the last line (Windows: cmd /c).
builtins.returns: Runs the command (Windows: via cmd /c); returns its last output line.

builtins.name: passthru
builtins.desc: Runs an external command and forwards its raw binary output to stdout.

builtins.name: RESET
builtins.desc: Colour constant: the terminal's default colour. Pass it as the second argument of print()/println()/input() to end a coloured line.
builtins.returns: The value of the first element.

builtins.name: BLACK
builtins.desc: Colour constant: black — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: RED
builtins.desc: Colour constant: red — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: GREEN
builtins.desc: Colour constant: green — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: YELLOW
builtins.desc: Colour constant: yellow — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BLUE
builtins.desc: Colour constant: blue — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: MAGENTA
builtins.desc: Colour constant: magenta — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: CYAN
builtins.desc: Colour constant: cyan — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: WHITE
builtins.desc: Colour constant: white — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_BLACK
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright black (dark grey) — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_RED
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright red — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_GREEN
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright green — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_YELLOW
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright yellow — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_BLUE
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright blue — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_MAGENTA
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright magenta — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_CYAN
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright cyan — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: BRIGHT_WHITE
builtins.desc: Colour constant: bright white — optional second argument of print()/println()/input().

builtins.name: print
builtins.desc: print($value[, $colour]) — writes to stdout without a newline. The optional second argument is one of the colour constants below.

builtins.name: println
builtins.desc: println($value[, $colour]) — like print() but ends the line. A colour wraps only this one line and is reset afterwards.

builtins.name: input
builtins.desc: input($prompt[, $colour]) — prints the prompt (optionally coloured), reads one line from stdin and returns it without the newline.

builtins.name: proc_open
builtins.desc: Starts an external process with separate pipes — advanced process control.

builtins.name: proc_get_status
builtins.desc: proc_get_status($h) — status array of a process started with proc_start() (still running, exit code, …).

builtins.name: proc_start
builtins.desc: proc_start($cmd[, $cwd]) — starts a process without blocking; returns its handle, or 0 when it could not start.

builtins.name: proc_read
builtins.desc: proc_read($h[, $max]) — what the process has written to stdout so far; empty string when nothing is pending.

builtins.name: proc_read_err
builtins.desc: proc_read_err($h[, $max]) — the same for stderr.

builtins.name: proc_write
builtins.desc: proc_write($h, $data) — writes to the process's stdin; returns the number of bytes written.

builtins.name: proc_alive
builtins.desc: proc_alive($h) — true while the process is still running.

builtins.name: proc_exit
builtins.desc: proc_exit($h) — exit code once it finished, -1 while it is still running.

builtins.name: proc_close
builtins.desc: proc_close($h) — releases the handle slot of a process.

builtins.name: proc_kill
builtins.desc: proc_kill($h) — terminates the process and its children.

builtins.name: ui_browser_ready
builtins.desc: true when the embedded Chromium runtime (WebView2) is available on this machine.

builtins.name: ui_browser_loader
builtins.desc: HTML of the loading splash shown while a page starts; empty string when none is set.

builtins.name: ui_browser_new
builtins.desc: ui_browser_new($parent, $dir) — creates an embedded browser inside a window; returns its handle.

builtins.name: ui_browser_free
builtins.desc: ui_browser_free($b) — destroys a browser handle.

builtins.name: ui_browser_fit
builtins.desc: ui_browser_fit($b, $top, $width) — resizes the browser area inside its window.

builtins.name: ui_browser_go
builtins.desc: ui_browser_go($b, $url) — navigates the browser to a URL.

builtins.name: ui_browser_html
builtins.desc: ui_browser_html($b, $html) — shows a document directly instead of loading a URL.

builtins.name: ui_browser_back
builtins.desc: Goes back in the session history.

builtins.name: ui_browser_forward
builtins.desc: Goes forward in the session history.

builtins.name: ui_browser_reload
builtins.desc: Reloads the current page.

builtins.name: ui_browser_stop
builtins.desc: Stops loading the current page.

builtins.name: ui_browser_can_back
builtins.desc: true when there is a page to go back to.

builtins.name: ui_browser_can_forward
builtins.desc: true when there is a page to go forward to.

builtins.name: ui_browser_url
builtins.desc: Current URL of the page.

builtins.name: ui_browser_favicon
builtins.desc: URL of the current page's favicon.

builtins.name: ui_browser_title
builtins.desc: Title of the current document.

builtins.name: ui_browser_zoom
builtins.desc: ui_browser_zoom($b, $factor) — sets the page zoom, 1.0 = 100 %.

builtins.name: ui_browser_zoom_get
builtins.desc: Current zoom factor of the browser.

builtins.name: ui_browser_devtools
builtins.desc: ui_browser_devtools($b, $on) — opens or closes the developer tools.

builtins.name: ui_browser_devtools_fit
builtins.desc: Keeps the browser area sized correctly while the devtools panel is docked.

builtins.name: ui_browser_devtools_ready
builtins.desc: true once the devtools window is up.

builtins.name: ui_browser_print
builtins.desc: Opens the print dialog for the current page.

builtins.name: ui_browser_post
builtins.desc: ui_browser_post($b, $url, …) — performs an HTTP POST from the browser context.

builtins.name: ui_browser_on
builtins.desc: ui_browser_on($b, $event, $callback) — registers a closure for browser events (navigation, load, …).

builtins.name: ui_browser_key
builtins.desc: ui_browser_key($b, $mod, $vk, $cmd, $callback) — binds a keyboard shortcut inside the browser.

builtins.name: ui_browser_visible
builtins.desc: ui_browser_visible($b, $on) — shows or hides the embedded browser.

builtins.name: thr_spawn
builtins.desc: thr_spawn($closure[, $args]) — runs the closure on a new thread; returns the thread id or false.

builtins.name: thr_join
builtins.desc: thr_join($tid) — waits for a spawned thread; true when it was still joinable.

builtins.name: thr_current
builtins.desc: Id of the calling thread.

builtins.name: thr_id
builtins.desc: OS-level id of the calling thread.

builtins.name: thr_sleep_ms
builtins.desc: thr_sleep_ms($ms) — sleeps the current thread.

builtins.name: thr_cpu_count
builtins.desc: Number of hardware threads — use it to size a worker pool.

builtins.name: thr_parallel_map
builtins.desc: thr_parallel_map($closure, $items[, $workers]) — maps the closure over the array on several threads and returns the results in order.

builtins.name: chan_new
builtins.desc: chan_new($capacity) — creates a channel; capacity 0 means unbuffered (rendezvous, Go style).

builtins.name: chan_send
builtins.desc: chan_send($ch, $value) — blocks until the value is taken; throws when the channel is closed.

builtins.name: chan_recv
builtins.desc: chan_recv($ch) — blocks for the next value; false once the channel is closed and drained.

builtins.name: chan_try_send
builtins.desc: Like chan_send() but returns false instead of blocking.

builtins.name: chan_try_recv
builtins.desc: Like chan_recv() but returns false instead of blocking.

builtins.name: chan_close
builtins.desc: Closes the channel: further sends fail, receives drain what is left and then return false.

builtins.name: mutex_new
builtins.desc: Creates a mutex and returns its id.

builtins.name: mutex_lock
builtins.desc: Locks the mutex, blocking until it is free.

builtins.name: mutex_trylock
builtins.desc: Locks the mutex only if it is free right now; false otherwise.

builtins.name: mutex_unlock
builtins.desc: Unlocks the mutex.

builtins.name: mutex_free
builtins.desc: Releases the mutex id for reuse.

builtins.name: barrier_new
builtins.desc: barrier_new($n) — creates a barrier that releases once n threads have arrived.

builtins.name: barrier_wait
builtins.desc: Waits at the barrier; returns the arrival index of the last thread to arrive.

builtins.name: atomic_new
builtins.desc: atomic_new([$init]) — creates an atomic int (default 0) and returns its id.

builtins.name: atomic_get
builtins.desc: Reads an atomic value.

builtins.name: atomic_set
builtins.desc: atomic_set($a, $value) — stores a value atomically.

builtins.name: atomic_add
builtins.desc: atomic_add($a, $delta) — adds and returns the previous value.

builtins.name: atomic_cas
builtins.desc: atomic_cas($a, $expect, $set) — compare-and-set; true when the value was $expect and became $set.

builtins.name: malloc
builtins.desc: unsafe: allocates n bytes of raw memory; returns a pointer for memcpy/memset/ffi. Must be freed with free().
builtins.returns: Raw pointer to n bytes (unsafe block required). Free with free().

builtins.name: free
builtins.desc: unsafe: frees a raw pointer obtained from FFI. Wrong use corrupts memory — this is why it needs an unsafe block.
builtins.returns: Frees the memory. Double-free = corruption; that is why this needs unsafe.

builtins.name: memcpy
builtins.desc: unsafe: copies $n bytes from one raw address to another.
builtins.returns: Copies $n raw bytes.

builtins.name: memset
builtins.desc: unsafe: fills $n bytes at an address with a byte value.
builtins.returns: Fills $n bytes with $byte.

builtins.name: ffi_load
builtins.desc: unsafe: ffi_load("mylib.dll") — loads a shared library for direct native calls. Returns a library handle or false.
builtins.returns: Library handle for ffi_call(), or false on failure. Requires unsafe.

builtins.name: ffi_call
builtins.desc: unsafe: ffi_call($lib, "symbol") — resolves an exported function in a loaded library; call the result with the documented signature.
builtins.returns: Callable for the native function. Requires unsafe.

builtins.name: heap_dump
builtins.desc: Returns a debug dump of the runtime heap (allocation count, sizes).
builtins.returns: Debug dump of the runtime heap (allocation count, sizes).

builtins.name: holy_maxout_start
builtins.desc: holy_maxout_start($port, $dbPath) — starts the bundled io_uring HTTP benchmark server (Linux only); returns the bound port or -1.

builtins.name: holy_challenge_start
builtins.desc: holy_challenge_start($port, $dbPath) — starts the bundled challenge HTTP server (Linux only); returns the bound port or -1.
